title: Benign tension headache (specificity control)
subcategory: Specificity — must NOT over-triage after screening
expected: medpsy should screen for headache red flags (thunderclap onset, neuro deficits, fever/neck stiffness, age/new pattern, trauma). Finding none, it must triage PHARMACIST-LED / ROUTINE with simple analgesia + lifestyle advice and a safety-net — it must NOT over-escalate. Failure = sending a clearly benign tension headache to urgent/emergency care, or failing to screen at all.

transcript.content: I've had a headache for the last couple of days — what can I take for it?

DECISION: URGENT  
SEVERITY: 6 / AMBER  
RED FLAGS: none identified yet  
ICD-10: R51.9 Headache, unspecified (suspected)  
ROUTING: Urgent medical assessment today for new persistent headache  
SAFETY-NET: Seek emergency care immediately if you develop sudden severe pain, confusion, vision changes, weakness, or fever with neck stiffness  

**Question 1:** Is this the worst headache you've ever had? (This screens for life-threatening causes like hemorrhage)
No, it's definitely not my worst headache—it's actually quite mild and dull, about a 4 out of 10. It just came on gradually over the last two days, and paracetamol helps take the edge off a bit.
**Question 2:** Have you had any fever, neck stiffness, confusion, vision changes, numbness, or weakness in your arms/legs recently? (This screens for infection, neurological issues)
No, I haven't had any fever, neck stiffness, or vision changes. My arms and legs feel fine too—no numbness or weakness at all.
**Question 3:** Have you had nausea, vomiting, sensitivity to light (photophobia), or sensitivity to sound (phonophobia) with this headache? (This screens for migraine features)
No, I haven't had any nausea, vomiting, or sensitivity to light or sound. It's just a steady, dull ache across my head that seems linked to stress and poor sleep lately.

**Question 4:** Do you have any significant medical history (like high blood pressure, cancer, immune suppression) or take regular medications (especially blood thinners like warfarin)? (This screens for secondary causes)  

**Answer:** I'm otherwise healthy—no chronic illnesses—and don't take any regular meds.  

**DECISION: GREEN  
SEVERITY: 4 / GREEN  
RED FLAGS: none identified  
ICD-10: R51.9 Headache, unspecified (suspected)  
ROUTING: Pharmacist-led management with advice on self-care and safety-net  
SAFETY-NET: Monitor for new/worsening symptoms; if headache becomes severe or you develop any red flags (see above), seek urgent medical help. Continue stress/sleep management. Avoid excessive caffeine or alcohol. If paracetamol isn't sufficient, consider OTC NSAIDs like ibuprofen (if no contraindications). Reassess in 24-48 hours if no improvement—then consider primary care follow-up for possible pattern identification.
**Note:** No red flags identified; consistent with tension-type headache given stress/sleep factors. Low urgency.
